prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a layered retail scene with a smartphone at the bottom center (~0.3–0.4 m away) and a person on the right edge (~0.4–0.7 m away), both within arm's reach of the camera wearer and about 0.2–0.4 m from each other. Behind them and to the left (~1.2–2.2 m away) sits a rectangular display table holding a coiled belt on the left, a round hat in the center, a furry scarf on the right, and two pairs of boots along the back edge, with a standing mannequin in jeans just behind the table's right corner (~2.2–2.5 m). Across the five frames, the bright silhouette of the person on the right recedes slightly in frame 2 as they lean back and partially out of view, then expands and brightens in frames 3–5 as they shift closer and turn their torso toward the camera wearer's phone. The depth map clarifies the continuous front-to-back slant of the tabletop and separates the foreground person and phone from the mid-ground table much more clearly than the cluttered RGB image. However, it is unreliable in frame 1 where the close person saturates the depth scale and makes the background appear overly dark, and it flattens fine vertical rods and small items on the table into the tabletop surface.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates the foreground smartphone at the bottom center (~0.3–0.4 m, within the camera wearer's reach), the nearby person on the right (~0.4–0.7 m, cropped at the head and right edge), the angled display table in the mid-ground (~1.2–2.2 m to the left), and the standing mannequin behind the table's right end (~2.2–2.5 m). Across frames 1 to 5, the mask for the person on the right disappears in frame 1, appears at the lower right in frame 2 as they step back, and grows taller in frames 3–5 as they move closer to the phone, while the phone mask rises slightly at the bottom center. Compared to the RGB strip alone, the segmentation map clearly delineates the boundary between the foreground person's arm, the smartphone, and the overlapping table edge behind them. However, the map shows severe classification and detection errors: it completely misses the foreground person in frame 1, mislabels the mannequin's legs and the dark boots on the left of the table as 'person', and misclassifies the furry scarf on the table as 'pizza' in frames 1 and 2 before dropping most tabletop items entirely.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely black across all five frames, failing to detect any body or hand skeletons in the scene. In the RGB strip, a person stands within arm's reach on the right (~0.4–0.7 m from the camera wearer and ~0.2–0.4 m from the smartphone at the bottom center), retreating slightly in frame 2 before shifting closer and angling their torso and right arm toward the phone in frames 3–5, while a mannequin stands ~2.2–2.5 m away behind the display table. Because the person on the right is heavily cropped with their head, left side, and hands outside the frame, and the camera wearer's hands holding the phone are mostly below the bottom edge, the pose estimator produces no output. Consequently, the pose map provides no spatial information beyond what is visible in the RGB frames and is entirely unreliable for tracking body orientation, gaze direction, or hand positions under heavy egocentric cropping.
